HP_UNITS_CORRECTION: HP is a u16 LITTLE-ENDIAN in 1/64 units. The "1/4 scale byte" in older docs is only the HIGH BYTE. Read 2 bytes at addr, not 1. Naruto 4-koma = 9216 raw = 144.0. Goku 10240 = 160.0. Luffy 9728 = 152.0. Anything reading one byte silently truncates - distrust prior sub-integer damage conclusions. Source: peer session, docs/research/HP-And-Damage-Runtime-Findings.md

nature_P1b_REFUTED: Nature is NOT a per-koma-indexed table anywhere in the ROM binaries. Exhaustive: every byte offset, 3 encodings (u8 / nibble / 2-bit), across arm9.bin + all 26 bin/ files + all 14 overlays. Zero candidates. nature_REFRAME: Deck-System.md says nature variants REUSE the same battle data and specials still use the base nature. So panel nature is NOT a combat property - it is deck-building only, used for deck bonuses. That means it need not sit near chr_b/chr_s at all, and only has to exist where the deck editor + deck-bonus calc run: the deckmake overlay data, or inside the .aar archives that only that mode loads.

METHOD_NOTE: THE GROUP IS THE SIGNATURE, NOT THE ELEMENT. My first nature scan used Naruto 9-panel nature pattern -> 224 candidates, all noise (in 2-bit data only 4 values exist so a 9-element equality pattern matches constantly). The 312-way invariant dropped it to zero. Harness hit the identical lesson in RAM: a single 0x50 slot matched 1167 times in 4MB, four consecutive slots at stride 0x50 was unique. A wide invariant beats a clever pattern.

combat_phase_entry_points.nature_in_combat: RESOLVED, and it is NOT the multiplier. 0x021540AA (ov06, Thumb) calls the nature predicate 0x02078CB8 purely to choose an ASSET FILENAME: predicate true -> "battle/chr/??_?_??_b.aar" with VRAM allowance 0x005F2000; false -> "battle/chr/??_?_??.aar" with 0x005F1000. So a panel with an explicit nature override loads the _b sprite archive - correct for the alternate-nature variants having different art. No damage arithmetic at the site. combat_phase_entry_points.damage_apply: 0x02078488 core (HP = clamp(current+delta,0,max)); public entry 0x020783CC; list variant 0x020783DC. 8 call sites in ov06 listed in state. Delta arrives ALREADY COMPUTED, so resistance is upstream - trace the producers of r1.
combat_phase_entry_points.method_note: Static value search finds TABLES. It cannot find FUNCTIONS. Reach for disassembly sooner in this phase - the koma sprint lost several iterations to that lesson.
combat_phase_entry_points.MY_ERROR_4: "In arm9.bin" does NOT mean "runs in this mode". arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic; only the CALLER identifies the mode. Use scripts/find_callers.py (peer) BEFORE assuming a function participates in a phase.
combat_phase_entry_points.METHOD_LESSON_SHARPENED: Value-space search cannot find a computation, AND text-grep cannot find an ABSENCE. "Zero callers" is only meaningful once you have the COMPLETE binary set - grepping the 9 dumped disasm files would have missed it, and overlays sharing a load address make "which file is this in?" ambiguous. The absence of a caller is as informative as the presence of one.
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_dispatcher: All 8 ov06 sites are handlers in a script-effect dispatcher shaped: ldr r1,[r1,#4] (effect record); ldrsh r1,[r1,#4] (signed halfword data parameter); lsl r1,r1,#6 (x64, displayed->raw); bl 0x020783CC. So damage values are AUTHORED IN DISPLAYED UNITS and scaled at the last moment. A sibling at 0x02159290 uses lsl #8 into a different stat - a family of "apply data parameter to stat X" handlers. NONE of the 8 contains resistance math; it is upstream in hit resolution, still not found.
combat_phase_entry_points.sub_integer_damage_discriminator: The measured 1.250 damage = 80 raw is NOT a multiple of 64, so it did NOT come through a lsl #6 handler. At least one damage path produces a genuine sub-integer value. Useful discriminator for locating that path.
combat_phase_entry_points.THREE_WAY_EPISTEMIC_NOTE: Worth keeping straight, because two separate things were wrong and they cancelled: (1) MY PREMISE WAS INVALID - "the function is in arm9.bin, therefore it runs in this mode" is not valid reasoning; arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic, and only the caller identifies the mode. (2) MY CONCLUSION WAS NONETHELESS CORRECT - nature really is read in ov06. (3) THE REFUTATION WAS ALSO WRONG - it rested on a BL decoder that handled only ARM (0xEB) and missed Thumb BL/BLX, so it manufactured a confident "zero callers in ov06". Do not collapse this into "my reasoning was fine after all". The reasoning was bad and the answer was lucky. Both facts stay on the record.
combat_phase_entry_points.LESSON_absence_claims: An ABSENCE claim silently inherits every gap in the method behind it. "Zero callers" is only as strong as the decoder is complete - and an absence is exactly the kind of claim a teammate propagates without re-verifying. What exposed the gap was a live GDB breakpoint capturing lr = 0x02150ddd: bit 0 set means the caller was THUMB. Treat all pre-fc56df9 caller counts from the peer as ARM-only until re-run.
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_bypass_SUGGESTIVE_NOT_PROVEN: Across 14736 breakpoint hits on the HP-apply function 0x02078488, EVERY delta was +128 (+2.0 displayed) from one Thumb caller - the training auto-heal, once per character per frame. ZERO negative deltas. BUT the peer could not confirm a melee hit landed during that window (the constant per-frame heal pins HP at max, so a damage dip is invisible), so this is SUGGESTIVE that melee damage bypasses 0x02078488, not proof.
combat_phase_entry_points.HP_APPLY_HAS_14_CALLERS_NOT_8: My Thumb-aware scan found SIX Thumb blx callers of 0x020783CC that the earlier ARM-only list missed: 0x02150DD8, 0x021513D8, 0x021513EE, 0x021514E6, 0x021515B2, 0x02151636 - plus the 8 known ARM sites. Exact match, so 0x02150DD8 is the training auto-heal caller they hit 14736 times.
combat_phase_entry_points.melee_damage_lead: The FIVE remaining new Thumb sites (0x021513D8, 0x021513EE, 0x021514E6, 0x021515B2, 0x02151636) are the best candidates for melee damage. The peer 14736-hit observation saw deltas from only ONE caller and suggested melee bypasses 0x02078488; a simpler explanation is that melee comes through one of these five previously-unknown sites and none fired because no melee hit landed in that window.
combat_phase_entry_points.TRIANGLE_CONFIRMED_IN_CODE: 0x02160944-0x021609B8 (ov06, ARM) loops over characters comparing nature at runtime struct +0x13 via chain [r2]->+0x118->+0x56C. DENOMINATOR.deviation_from_plan: The plan said bucket functions by ADDRESS RANGE. That cannot work: ten overlays load at 0x0214CD20, so range-bucketing would multiply-count every overlay function. functions.json already has a provenance field naming the source binary, so I attribute by provenance and use address ranges only as a consistency check (which passes - no function falls outside its claimed window).

DENOMINATOR.COMBAT_DENOMINATOR: battle-specific surface is AT LEAST 1622 functions (ov6 752 + ov11 234 + ov12 636) = ~19% of all identified functions. How much of arm9 4043 belongs to battle is UNKNOWN from this data - see the limitation below.
DENOMINATOR.CRITICAL_LIMITATION: The call graph in functions.json is INTRA-BINARY ONLY. Of 13809 caller edges, ZERO cross a binary boundary. Ground truth proving the gap: 0x020783CC (HP-delta apply) has 8 callers all in ov6 (harness verified by decoding BL across every binary), functions.json records none of them AND does not list that address as a function at all. Consequence: caller/callee data CANNOT establish which mode uses an arm9 function. This is the SAME blind spot that produced my "in arm9 therefore runs in battle" error. Any "which mode calls this?" question needs a cross-binary call graph built by decoding BL out of the binaries - not by grepping the text disassembly, which only covers the files someone dumped.
DENOMINATOR.next_tool_worth_building: A cross-binary call graph over arm9 + all 14 overlays would give the real combat denominator and fix the connectivity blind spot. The harness peer has scripts/find_callers.py which does this for a given address list; scaling it to all 8712 functions is the obvious follow-up.

2. Determine what the +0x40 byte gate is and what [r5,#0x34] points at (a koma record? the predicate takes koma+0xB flags).
3. Follow the branch taken when the predicate returns true vs false - a nature multiplier would appear as a multiply/shift on a damage or stat value in one arm.
4. Cross-check against the 8 known ov6 damage sites; if the nature branch feeds any of them, that is the resistance/multiplier path the peer cannot find from the delta side.

regen_confirmed: My regen tip confirmed twice: struct +0x49 (= hp_addr +0x31) read 1, and poking it to 0 stopped healing dead. Cleaner route is the menu 自動回復 OFF, which makes damage cumulative (verified 10240 -> 8704 from two hits, held). Subtlety: menu OFF leaves +0x49 still reading 1, so the setting gates whether the regen ROUTINE RUNS rather than zeroing the rate - two mechanisms, same observable. Arithmetic closes: rate 1 -> 1*2=2 displayed -> *64 = 128 raw, matching the +128 deltas.
